title: Credit Card Balances at Pace with Inflation: Whitney
summary: Meredith Whitney, CEO of Meredith Whitney Advisory Group, joins Scarlet Fu and Tom Keene on "Bloomberg Money." They discuss how many Americans are living payday to payday as well as how consumers are utilizing their credit cards. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Short-Term Treasuries Cap Biggest Weekly Rally Since May on Data
summary: US Treasuries rallied after an unexpectedly weak July employment report prompted traders to further dial back expectations for Federal Reserve interest-rate hikes, cementing the biggest weekly gain in short-term maturities since May.

title: Latest Oil Market News and Analysis for Aug. 7
summary: Oil steadied as tensions in the Middle East flared while traders monitored progress toward a deal between Iran and Oman to restore shipping through the Strait of Hormuz.

title: Gold Jumps as Weak US Jobs Data Adds Fuel to Bullion’s Rebound
summary: Gold jumped more than 3% after an unexpected contraction in the US jobs market, extending a rebound from its slump below $4,000 an ounce.

title: PGA Is Not Talking to LIV Golf About a Merger, Commissioner Says
summary: Brian Rolapp, CEO of PGA Tour, joins Scarlet Fu and Tom Keene on "Bloomberg Money." They discuss the changing landscape of sports media coverage, the rising costs of streaming bills for consumers, and the evolution of the PGA Tour. He also says there are no plans at all to merge with the struggling LIV Golf tour. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Stocks Rise After Jobs, Oil Falls on US-Iran Hopes: Markets Wrap
summary: A sharp slowdown in the US jobs market drove stocks higher while bond yields fell on speculation the Federal Reserve won’t be forced to raise interest rates any time soon.

title: Investing View is Glass 'More Than Half-Full': Kelly
summary: David Kelly, Chief Global Strategist at JPMorgan Asset Management, joins Scarlet Fu and Tom Keene on "Bloomberg Money." They discuss how biased information influences investor behavior.  (Source: Bloomberg)

title: NYC Deputy Mayor on Jobs, Taxes, Grocery Stores
summary: Julie Su, New York City deputy mayor for economic justice, talks about creating jobs, a new business advisory council, city-run grocery stores and Mayor Zohran Mamdani’s new  pied-à-terre tax on second homes. More than 31,000 property owners may get a new bill in the mail. She speaks to Bloomberg's Romaine Bostick. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: US Sues Kahn on Hedge Fund Collapse, Indicts Executive
summary: The US Securities and Exchange Commission sued Brian Kahn, the former head of Franchise Group Inc., over the collapse of a hedge fund that he helped run, and federal prosecutors criminally charged an executive at the fund in the matter.

title: Odd Lots: What It’s Like to Collaborate With Big Brand Names
summary:
In the age of brand collaborations, how do companies work together to benefit from each other's influence?

On this episode of the Odd Lots podcast, Fishwife CEO Becca Millstein joins Tracy Alloway and Joe Weisenthal to talk about the company's partnership with brands like Whole Foods and Fly By Jing. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: How the Food Industry Is Dealing With the Cyclospora Outbreak
summary:
Since Taco Bell was linked to the cyclospora outbreak, the fast food chain removed the allegedly implicated lettuce from its supply chain and, in a bid to win back hesitant diners, began offering special discounts on a concoction known as the Enchirito.

Bloomberg Businessweek's Deena Shanker joins Max Chafkin and Stacey Vanek Smith on the Everybody's Business podcast to discuss how the food industry is dealing with the growing health crisis. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Treasuries Rally as Soft Jobs Data Trims Fed Rate-Hike Bets
summary:
US Treasuries rallied after data showed employers unexpectedly cut jobs in July, suggesting labor market challenges that could impact the Federal Reserve’s willingness to raise interest rates.

The yield on two-year US Treasuries, which are sensitive to near-term moves in Fed monetary policy, fell as much as nine basis points on Friday to 4.15% as traders cut bets on interest-rate hikes in the coming months. The moves were pared later in the New York trading session as oil rose, though the two-year yield remained about four basis points lower on the day near 4.20%. We get reaction from Tom Tzitzouris, Head of Fixed Income Research at Baird Strategas. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Cyclospora Outbreak Sends Shivers Through Restaurant Stocks
summary: The cyclospora outbreak in the U.S. tied to lettuce used in restaurants has made more than 10,000 people sick according to the Centers for Disease Control. This has caused fewer people to go out to eat or get fast food. Now this is starting to hurt the restaurant sector. R.J. Hottovy of Placer.ai research covers the space and joins "Bloomberg The Close." (Source: Bloomberg)

title: US Stocks Pare Gains as Jobs Data Seen Easing Fed Rate Hike
summary: US stocks pared gains on Friday after jobs data showed the US economy unexpectedly shed jobs in July, which could prompt the Federal Reserve to delay interest-rate increases.

title: Phelan Confirmed to Lead Trump’s Council of Economic Advisers
summary: The US Senate confirmed Christopher Phelan, a former adviser to the Federal Reserve Bank of Minneapolis, as chairman of the White House Council of Economic Advisers.

title: Once-AAA Bonds on New York Megamall Face $350 Million Loss
summary: Pyramid Management Group, a shopping center developer, is buying back the mortgage on a struggling megamall it owns in Syracuse, New York, for cents on the dollar, mostly wiping out bonds that originally carried top ratings.

title: DraftKings Blasts Prediction Bets on Earnings Calls Comments
summary: DraftKings Inc. Chief Executive Officer Jason Robins said he doesn’t think it is good that bettors are placing prediction market wagers on what executives say on company earnings calls.

title: Big Tech Stocks Storm Back as AI Fears Fade and Euphoria Resumes
summary: After spending much of the year in the stock market doghouse over fears about their profligate spending on artificial intelligence, the world’s biggest technology companies are suddenly leading the way once again.

title: US Treasury Sparks Debate Over Auction Cutbacks to Temper Yields
summary: The US Treasury triggered debate this week about something that’s for years been an article of faith about the world’s biggest bond market: the government’s auctions of notes and bonds will just have to keep getting bigger.

title: The Free Money AI Bond Buildout Is Gone
summary: Hyperscaler debt funding is getting pricier.
